outcomeTiers.explanation: You navigated something genuinely difficult without losing yourself, or either friendship, in the process. That's rarer than it sounds.
It got messy, but you came through with both friendships more or less intact — bruised, not broken.
You stayed neutral when neutral wasn't really available. Something in one of these friendships is going to take a while to settle.
You said the easy thing every time it mattered, and it cost you the trust of someone who needed you to be honest.

establish.message: Jordan's been your closest friend since your first week at university — the kind of friendship where you've never really had to explain yourself. They picked you up at 2am the night your mum went into hospital. You were there when they lost their job and didn't leave the flat for a week. Jordan and Alex have been together for four years now. You introduced them, actually — Alex was your friend first. The three of you have become the kind of unit where nobody has to choose sides because there aren't any. Tonight's just another Saturday, everyone winding down after a long evening — until the room empties out and it's just the two of you.

choices.label: Continue

start.message: Jordan catches you alone in the kitchen after everyone else has drifted off. Their voice is lower than usual. "Can I tell you something? I just... need you not to judge me before I've even said it."

data.location: Kitchen, after everyone else has left

choices.label: Of course. Whatever it is, I'm listening.

reasons.savvy: You read that Jordan needed to feel safe before they could be honest.
reasons.streetSmarts: Meeting someone with openness usually earns you the real story, not a filtered one.
reasons.integrity: Offering that before you even know what's coming is its own kind of trust.

choices.label: That depends what it is.

reasons.streetSmarts: Conditional listening tends to get a conditional, guarded answer back.

confession.message: Jordan takes a breath. "I kissed someone. At the work conference last month. It's over — it happened once, I ended it immediately, I haven't spoken to them since. I just... I can't lose Alex over this. Please don't say anything."

choices.label: I won't say anything — but you need to tell Alex yourself, and soon.

reasons.savvy: You separated 'I'll keep your confidence' from 'I'll help you hide this.'
reasons.streetSmarts: You held the line without becoming the messenger between two people.
reasons.integrity: You didn't just promise silence — you named what actually needs to happen.

choices.label: How could you do that to Alex?

reasons.savvy: Your reaction was honest, even if it wasn't what Jordan needed to hear.
reasons.streetSmarts: Leading with judgment when someone's already frightened tends to shut a conversation down.
reasons.integrity: Not pretending to be fine with it is its own kind of honesty.

choices.label: That's between you and Alex. I'm staying out of it.

reasons.savvy: Calling it 'between them' missed that Jordan just made it about you by telling you.
reasons.streetSmarts: Staying out of it protects you, at least for now.
reasons.integrity: Neutrality isn't the same as not having a position — it's just not saying it.

confession_guarded.message: Jordan hesitates, then says it anyway — but faster, flatter, like they're pulling back even as the words come out. "I kissed someone at the conference. Once. It's done. I just needed to tell someone. Forget I said anything."

choices.label: Wait — I didn't mean to shut you down. Talk to me.

reasons.savvy: You noticed you'd pushed Jordan away and course-corrected.
reasons.streetSmarts: Reopening the conversation recovered ground the first response lost.
reasons.integrity: Admitting you responded badly took more than just listening would have.

choices.label: Okay. If that's what you want.

reasons.savvy: Jordan told you they forgot the sentence — they clearly didn't. You let it drop anyway.
reasons.integrity: Taking 'forget I said anything' at face value when someone is clearly hurting is a kind of complicity.

jordan_reacts_hold.message: Jordan nods slowly. "Yeah. I know. I know I need to." They look at you for a long moment. "Just... not yet. Give me a few weeks. I'll find the right time." There's genuine relief in their face — not because you agreed to keep quiet, but because you didn't make them feel like a terrible person for saying it out loud.

choices.label: Continue

jordan_reacts_judge.message: Jordan's face hardens. "I knew you'd react like this." They stand up, moving toward the door. "This is exactly why I almost didn't tell you." The kitchen suddenly feels a lot smaller.

choices.label: Wait. I'm sorry — that came out wrong. Sit down.

reasons.savvy: You caught that your delivery was doing damage and adjusted.
reasons.streetSmarts: Repairing the moment before Jordan walked out saved the conversation.
reasons.integrity: Apologising for how you said it without taking back what you meant.

choices.label: I'm not going to pretend this is fine, Jordan.

reasons.integrity: You held your ground even when it was clearly costing you.
reasons.streetSmarts: Being right and being effective aren't the same thing in this moment.

jordan_reacts_neutral.message: Jordan stares at you. "Right. Yeah. Between me and Alex." They pick up their glass, finish it. "Thanks for... yeah." The silence after that is the loudest thing in the room.

choices.label: Continue

reveal_calm.message: Three weeks later, Alex pulls you aside at a dinner, grinning so hard they can barely keep it together. "I'm going to propose. To Jordan. I've been looking at rings for months. I want you to help me pick the place — you know them better than anyone." Alex is watching your face, waiting for you to be as excited as they are.

data.location: Alex's living room, three weeks later

choices.label: That's amazing. Of course I'll help.

reasons.streetSmarts: You kept the moment steady instead of letting your face give anything away.
reasons.integrity: Matching Alex's excitement while sitting on this isn't neutral — it's a small performance.

choices.label: Are you sure the timing feels right? Like, really sure?

reasons.savvy: You found a way to introduce doubt without revealing anything you'd promised to keep.
reasons.integrity: That question was honest, even if Alex doesn't know why you're asking it.

choices.label: I need a second. That's... a lot to take in.

reasons.integrity: You didn't fake a reaction you didn't have.
reasons.streetSmarts: That pause is the kind of thing Alex might remember later and wonder about.

reveal_tense.message: Three weeks later, Alex pulls you aside, grinning. "I'm going to propose to Jordan. I want your help picking the place." You're still carrying what Jordan told you — and still angry about it — and it's hard to separate that from what's happening in front of you.

data.location: Alex's living room, three weeks later

choices.label: That's incredible. I'm so happy for you.

reasons.integrity: Enthusiasm you don't feel, aimed at someone who has no idea what you know, is a heavier lie than it looks.

choices.label: Alex... there's something you should probably know.

reasons.savvy: You read that Alex was about to make a permanent decision on incomplete information.
reasons.streetSmarts: Breaking the promise costs you Jordan — possibly for good.
reasons.integrity: You chose Alex's right to know over Jordan's wish to hide.

choices.label: Honestly, I need a minute.

reasons.integrity: You didn't perform happiness you didn't have.
reasons.streetSmarts: That reaction is going to raise questions you can't fully answer.

reveal_cold.message: Three weeks later, you're at a group dinner. Alex catches your eye across the table, mouths 'come here,' and pulls you into the hallway. "I'm proposing. Next month. Ring's already bought." They say it like it's the best secret in the world. You realise you're now carrying two.

choices.label: That's wonderful. I'm happy for you both.

reasons.integrity: You are now actively helping someone propose to a person you know cheated on them.
reasons.savvy: You're not reading the situation — you're avoiding it.

choices.label: Before you do... can we talk about something?

reasons.savvy: Better late than never — you're finally acknowledging what you've been carrying.
reasons.integrity: Re-engaging with something you'd walked away from took more than staying out of it did.

jordan_final_calm.message: Jordan finds you a few days later, quieter than usual. "I heard Alex is planning something. Should I tell them before they do it? Before they do something like... propose?" They're asking you directly this time. No hedging.

choices.label: Yes. Before Alex does anything, not after.
choices.consequence: It's a hard few weeks. But the proposal doesn't happen on a lie, and that was the thing that mattered. Jordan comes back eventually. Alex stays. It's different now — quieter, more careful. But it's honest.

reasons.savvy: You read that 'before' mattered more than 'gently.'
reasons.integrity: You gave the same honest answer you'd been building toward the whole time.
reasons.streetSmarts: Timing this before the proposal kept the damage as contained as it could be.

choices.landing: Jordan texts two days later: 'I told him.' Nothing else. You don't reply. You don't need to.

choices.label: That's your call. I can't make it for you.
choices.consequence: Nobody fought. Nobody lied outright. And nobody told the truth either. The proposal happened. Jordan never brought it up again. Neither did you.

reasons.integrity: Neutral wasn't dishonest, but it also wasn't the clarity Jordan was actually asking for.

choices.landing: The engagement photos go up on a Sunday evening. You scroll past them. Then scroll back. Then put your phone face-down on the table.

choices.label: I think you already know what you should do.
choices.consequence: Things are different now. Not broken — just not the same. The friendship is still there. It just learned something about itself it can't unlearn.

reasons.streetSmarts: Handing the question back protected you from the middle of it, but it also left Jordan alone with it.

choices.landing: Jordan texts a week later: 'I told Alex. It's bad.' You stare at the message. You type something. Delete it. Type again. Delete it.

jordan_final_tense.message: Jordan corners you, tense. "I know you're angry with me. But I heard something's coming with Alex. Should I say something before it happens?" There's an edge in their voice — they know exactly how you feel about this.

choices.label: Yes. And you should have already.
choices.consequence: Jordan tells Alex. The conversation with Alex is honest. The one between you and Jordan takes much longer to recover. But Alex never had to find out from someone who wasn't in the room.

reasons.integrity: The advice was right even though the delivery cost you something with Jordan.
reasons.streetSmarts: Being right and being kind aren't the same move, and you picked right.

choices.landing: You get a text from Alex a month later. Just: 'Thank you.' You read it three times.

choices.label: This isn't about my anger. Tell them.
choices.consequence: Your own anger takes longer to fade than the crisis itself did. But separating your feelings from the advice was the hardest thing you did in this whole mess — and probably the most important.

reasons.savvy: You separated your own feelings from the actual stakes for Jordan and Alex.
reasons.integrity: You gave the honest answer even while carrying your own reaction.

choices.landing: Jordan tells Alex. You hear about it secondhand. Nobody calls you.

choices.label: I'm still too annoyed to be objective about this.
choices.consequence: The proposal happened. You were there. You smiled in the photos. You went home and sat in the quiet for a long time.

reasons.integrity: At least it was honest about where you stood.
reasons.streetSmarts: It also left Jordan with no real answer at the exact moment they needed one.

choices.landing: At the engagement party, Alex squeezes your arm. 'Thanks for always being there for us.' You excuse yourself to the bathroom. You stand there for a while.

jordan_final_cold.message: You don't hear from Jordan about it at all. Two weeks later, Alex proposes. Jordan says yes. The engagement photos go up that evening. Your phone buzzes — it's Jordan: "Thanks for not saying anything. I owe you one." You stare at the message for a long time.

data.location: Your flat, alone, staring at your phone

choices.label: You don't owe me anything. I should have said something.
choices.consequence: You attend the engagement party. You smile in the photos. You go home. Some things you carry because you chose to. Some things you carry because you didn't choose not to.

reasons.integrity: Saying it now doesn't undo anything — but it's the first honest thing you've said since the kitchen.
reasons.savvy: You finally acknowledged what staying silent actually meant.

choices.landing: Jordan doesn't respond for two days. When they do, it's just: 'I know.'

choices.consequence: Nobody in the room knows what you know. You've become someone who carries this now — and you're not sure when you decided to be.

reasons.integrity: A heart emoji as a response to 'thanks for helping me hide an affair from the person I'm marrying' is about as far from honest as this scenario gets.
reasons.savvy: You're not staying out of it. You're in it — you've just convinced yourself you're not.

choices.landing: You give a speech at the engagement party. It's a good speech. Everyone laughs in the right places. You drive home alone.

alex_reacts_told.message: Alex stares at you. The grin is gone. They don't say anything for what feels like a very long time. Then, quietly: "How long have you known?"

choices.label: A few weeks. Jordan told me the night of the dinner.

reasons.savvy: You gave Alex the full picture instead of managing what they heard.
reasons.integrity: The timeline is uncomfortable, but Alex deserved the whole truth, not an edited version.

choices.label: It doesn't matter how long. What matters is you know now.

reasons.savvy: Alex asked a direct question and you redirected instead of answering it.
reasons.integrity: Controlling what Alex gets to know about this is what Jordan was doing too.

choices.label: Too long. I should have told you sooner.

reasons.integrity: Taking responsibility for the delay, not just for the telling, is the harder honesty.
reasons.streetSmarts: Admitting you sat on it opens you up to Alex's anger about the wait, not just the news.

alex_processes.message: Alex stands up. Walks to the window. Stands there with their back to you for a while. "I was going to propose. Did you know that too?" You nod. Alex lets out a breath that sounds like it's been held for weeks. "Right." They turn around. Their eyes are red but their voice is steady. "I need you to leave now. But..." A pause. "Thank you. For not letting me do that without knowing."

choices.label: You leave.

jordan_aftermath_told.message: Your phone rings an hour later. It's Jordan. You can hear they've been crying before they even speak. "Alex just called me. They know." A long silence. "Did you tell them?" Another silence. "I trusted you."

choices.label: I know. And I'm sorry. But Alex was about to propose to someone who was hiding something from them.
choices.consequence: Alex and Jordan don't get back together. But Alex stays in your life — closer than before, in a way that only happens when someone knows you chose them over comfort. Jordan comes back eventually. It's different. Quieter. But it's real.

reasons.integrity: You owned the decision without apologising for the principle behind it.
reasons.savvy: You named the exact reason — the proposal, not the kiss — that made waiting no longer an option.

choices.landing: Three months of silence. Then a text from Jordan: 'I still think you should have let me do it myself. But I understand why you didn't.'

choices.label: You gave me something I couldn't carry, Jordan. I tried.
choices.consequence: The friendship with Jordan doesn't end with a fight. It ends with a distance that neither of you closes. You think about calling sometimes. You don't.

reasons.integrity: You were honest about your own limits without making it Jordan's fault for having a secret.
reasons.savvy: Naming what actually happened — that the burden was unfair — is truer than either an apology or a justification.

choices.landing: Alex texts a week later: 'I don't blame you. I'm glad someone told me.' Jordan doesn't text at all.

choices.label: I'm sorry.
choices.consequence: Alex is hurt but relieved. Jordan is hurt and not relieved. You're somewhere in between. You wouldn't do it differently. But you'd do it better.

reasons.streetSmarts: An apology without any framing leaves Jordan with nothing to hold onto except the betrayal.

choices.landing: You sit in the silence after Jordan hangs up. The flat has never been this quiet.
